glosses: so, dass etwas durch Gegenbeispiel, Beobachtung oder Experiment widerlegt werden kann

examples.text: „Eine Aussage ist dann falsifizierbar, wenn es einen Beobachtungssatz gibt, mit dem die Aussage angreifbar ist. Trifft der Beobachtungssatz zu, ist die Aussage widerlegt.“

translations.source_sense_description: so, dass es falsifiziert werden kann

glosses: Logically capable of being proven false.

examples.text: The sentence "It will rain tomorrow" is falsifiable, while the sentence "It is what it is" is not.

glosses: Capable of being faked or forged.

examples.text: A digital signature algorithm must be not falsifiable.

glosses: The demarcation criterion between scientific and non-scientific statements proposed by Karl Popper. In order to be ranked as scientific, statements or systems of statements must be contradicted by an intersubjective singular existential statement, also called a basic statement, and not be contradicted by another, that is, they must also be logically possible.

examples.text: The statement It rains every day, everywhere is falsifiable, because it is contradicted by the basic statement On the third of August, in New York city it was not raining and it is not contradicted by the basic statement On the second of August, in New York city it was raining, while the statement It will rain someday is not falsifiable.

translations.source_sense_description: so, dass es falsifiziert werden kann
